Entry Golden Empire of Yi Ti Yi Di is often called the Golden Empire, and its rulers express the order of the world with divine imperial power, wealth, and the magnificence of the capital. It is easy for outsiders to understand "gold" only as gold and silver, but the political imagination of the Yi people regards it as the same as the destiny, ritual system, agriculture and the cities' influence on the central government. Altars, relics, and prophecies can unite people and give a political claim the appearance of irrefutability.

Entry Golden Empire of Yi Ti Yi Di is often called the Golden Empire, and its rulers express the order of the world with divine imperial power, wealth, and the magnificence of the capital. It is easy for outsiders to understand "gold" only as gold and silver, but the political imagination of the Yi people regards it as the same as the destiny, ritual system, agriculture and the cities' influence on the central government. Some people use it as a talisman, while others use it as the name of fear; the same prayer may make people draw their swords or put them down.

Entry Golden Empire of Yi Ti Yi Di is often called the Golden Empire, and its rulers express the order of the world with divine imperial power, wealth, and the magnificence of the capital. It is easy for outsiders to understand "gold" only as gold and silver, but the political imagination of the Yi people regards it as the same as the destiny, ritual system, agriculture and the cities' influence on the central government. Whether the gods responded or not could not be proven by the account books, but how the rituals were held and who could interpret the omens actually determined the authority of the community.

It is easy for outsiders to understand "gold" only as gold and silver, but the political imagination of the Yi people regards it as the same as the destiny, ritual system, agriculture and the cities' influence on the central government. They seek an explanation they can rely on when it comes to birth, marriage, sowing, illness, and death; the names of gods may not be the same, but their desire to keep their families safe is similar.
